questions.title: Filter and sort
questions.prompt: List the name and start_year of every student in the MIDS program. Sort by start_year (oldest first), then by name A to Z.
questions.hint_sql:
SELECT name, start_year
FROM students
WHERE program = 'MIDS'
ORDER BY start_year, name;

questions.title: Count per group
questions.prompt: How many courses does each department offer? Return department and course_count. Put the largest count first; break ties by department A to Z.
questions.hint_sql:
SELECT department, COUNT(*) AS course_count
FROM courses
GROUP BY department
ORDER BY course_count DESC, department;

questions.title: Join three tables
questions.prompt: Who is enrolled in IDS 706 in Fall 2026? Return each student's name and program, sorted by name A to Z.
questions.hint_sql:
SELECT s.name, s.program
FROM enrollments e
JOIN students s ON s.student_id = e.student_id
JOIN courses  c ON c.course_id  = e.course_id
WHERE c.course_code = 'IDS 706'
  AND e.term = 'Fall 2026'
ORDER BY s.name;

questions.title: Aggregate with HAVING
questions.prompt: Consider only completed enrollments (grade_points is not NULL). Find students who have completed at least 3 courses with an average grade_points of 3.5 or higher. Return name, courses_completed and avg_grade_points rounded to 2 decimals. Sort by avg_grade_points (highest first), then name A to Z.
questions.hint_sql:
SELECT s.name,
       COUNT(*) AS courses_completed,
       ROUND(AVG(e.grade_points), 2) AS avg_grade_points
FROM enrollments e
JOIN students s ON s.student_id = e.student_id
WHERE e.grade_points IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.student_id, s.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 AND AVG(e.grade_points) >= 3.5
ORDER BY avg_grade_points DESC, s.name;

questions.title: Top student per course (window function)
questions.prompt: For each course, find the student(s) with the highest grade_points among completed enrollments. If several students tie for the top grade, include all of them. Return course_code, name and grade_points, sorted by course_code, then name.
questions.hint_sql:
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT c.course_code, s.name, e.grade_points,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.course_id
                        ORDER BY e.grade_points DESC) AS rnk
    FROM enrollments e
    JOIN students s ON s.student_id = e.student_id
    JOIN courses  c ON c.course_id  = e.course_id
    WHERE e.grade_points IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT course_code, name, grade_points
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY course_code, name;
